model: INMBSTOS001R000 Toshiba AC to Modbus RTU gateway
applies_to: Toshiba Digital Inverter (RAV) and VRF indoor units on the AB remote bus via INMBSTOS001R0xx, user manual r2.9 (01/2024).
summary: Modbus RTU server on the AB remote-controller bus of Toshiba Digital Inverter (RAV) and VRF indoor units. Basic holding registers cover on/off, mode, fan, vane, setpoint, room temperature, alarm and error code; with a unit type chosen on SW1 it also exposes per-indoor-unit diagnostics such as room and suction temperatures, defrost and filter alarm.

addressing.note: Tables give a 'protocol address' (base 0) and a 'PLC address' (base 1); the protocol address is the wire address. Per-indoor-unit diagnostics are printed as a formula, (IU - 1) * 25 + 4000 + n; this file lists IU 1 only (4000-4021, without 4013-4015 and 4018-4019). For IU 2 add 25, and so on.

source.title: Intesis INMBSTOS001R0xx Modbus RTU (EIA-485) Interface for Toshiba air conditioners - User's Manual

notes: Every register is documented as a 16-bit unsigned holding register and no temperature range in the manual goes below zero, so temperatures are UINT16. The 'no value' marker the manual writes as -32768 is raw 0x8000 (32768) and is listed as an enum entry. Temperature registers depend on DIP SW4: x1 °C, x10 °C (decidegrees) or °F (no °F x10). The register-table footnote calls x10 the default, but the SW4 table and the quick-start page (all other switches off) give x1 °C as the factory setting, so scale 1 / °C is used. Read SW4 position 1-2 on site: if x10 is set use scale 0.1; if °F is set the values are whole °F.
Advanced diagnostic temperatures (4010-4012, 4016, 4021) are printed as 'x1 °C' and kept as UINT16 per the manual; the manual never says how a sub-zero value would be encoded.
Left out: indoor fan-coil temperatures TCJ, TC2 and TC1 (4013-4015). Coil temperatures can fall below 0 °C and the manual gives no signed encoding for these unsigned registers.
Left out because the printed scale is ambiguous: indoor PMV opening ('x1, x10 Pulses', 4018) and running hours indoor fan ('x100 hours', 4019).

Left out: outdoor-unit diagnostic blocks for VRF-SMMSi (4200+), VRF-SHRM/SMMS and RAV systems. They mix 'x10 A', 'X100 MPa', 'x10 RPS' and 'x100 hours' notations whose direction (multiply or divide) is not defined, and outdoor temperatures can go below zero with no signedness stated.
Advanced registers are only populated when SW1 selects a unit type other than the default; the Priority column (0 start-up, 1 high, 2 low) sets how often each is refreshed, tuned with register 4451.
Error code enum (Toshiba codes) not reproduced; see manual section 7.
Register 5 is marked R/W in the register table but described as read-only in the temperature section; it is listed read-only here. Use register 22 to supply an external temperature.
Default slave address: the quick-start page and register 15 range (1..63) give 1, while the SW3 table labels the all-off position (address 0) as default. Unit ID 1 is listed; check SW3 on site.

integration.summary: Leave SW1 at the defaults for plain control (gateway is AB-bus master), set address and baud on SW3/SW4, power-cycle, then poll holding registers 0-11 with function 03 and write with 06. Select RAV or VRF on SW1 only if you need the 4000+ diagnostics.
integration.enable: No enable step; register 7 (gateway disablement) must be 0 for commands to reach the unit.
quirks: Diagnostic addresses are per indoor unit: (IU - 1) * 25 + 4000 + offset.
Register 5 reads the Modbus-supplied temperature (reg 22) when one is valid, and is offset ±0.5 °C by mode.
setup: SW1: indoor unit type (default 'not specified'; RAV / VRF SMMS / VRF SHRM enable diagnostics) and AB-bus role (master by default; slave if a Toshiba remote is the header).
SW3: slave address; SW3/SW4: baud (9600 default).
DIP changes need a power cycle.
gotchas: Writes made while the gateway is still initialising are not applied; some registers read undetermined values until start-up completes.
Error code 65535 means the gateway lost the indoor unit.
